title: kernels-kvcache-batching-weekly-standup-log
content:
Week summary (Mar 9–12)

High level: this week we focused on three converging efforts: kernel selection/autotuning for medium-length sequences, KV cache eviction/diagnostics, and improving continuous-batching latency tail for mixed workloads. Small wins across the board: a new fused softmax microkernel produced consistent 6–9% median latency improvement on V100, and the new cache hit-rate metrics let us safely enable prefix cache for two additional model families (gpt-medium-v2, redwood-compat-7b).

Major outcomes
- Kernels: merged PR #842 (fused-softmax + tile-size autotuner) to canary; initial canary on dedicated-gpu-2 shows 7% med token latency improvement, 3% p95 improvement for seq_len=512 workloads. PR #855 (fast-attn fallback path) is still WIP—profiling shows regressions on small batches which we're addressing.
- KV cache: implemented TTL + sharded LRU prototype. Measured hit-rate uplift from 18% -> 37% for chat session logs (prefix-heavy requests). Memory overhead reasonable (~1.8GB per 16GB partition). Enabled additional diagnostics (cache_hit_rate, eviction_rate, avg_kv_age) in /metrics/serving/runtime/kvcache.
- Batching: deployed a small change to the continuous-batching heuristic that favors shorter requests when tail latency exceeds 1.2x SLO. This reduced p99 for mixed-short workloads by ~14% on staging.

Daily standups (high-level notes)
Mon 2026-03-09
- Priya: validated fused-softmax microkernel on A100 and V100; saw perf variance on A100 for seq_len <= 64. Filed issue JIRA-RT-356.
- Lina: landed cache metrics and started dashboard; saw initial cache hit jump on a replayed workload.
- Benji: investigated small-batch regression in fast-attn fallback; narrowed to tile-size interaction with cuBLAS path.
- Maya: ran end-to-end correctness tests for quantization path (int4 path) with KV cache enabled; minor mismatch in token sampling RNG under quantized path when KV hits are hot.

Tue 2026-03-10
- Priya: autotuner now stores per-device best-tile in a compact table persisted to local disk; smoke-tested restart recovery.
- Benji: wrote microbench harness to compare cuBLAS vs custom kernel for batch sizes 1–8; sent initial numbers to #eng-runtime.
- Samir: started drafting rollout plan for enabling KV cache for redwood-compat-7b; needs sign-off on memory guardrails.

Wed 2026-03-11
- Team sync: discussed canary metrics and rollback thresholds. Agreed to rollback if p95 increases by >5% or error rate increases by >0.2% during first 1h of canary.
- Lina: dashboard now has hourly breakdown of cache hit rate by customer and model family. Observed one tenant with a pathological access pattern — opened support ticket.
- Maya: confirmed RNG mismatch root cause — off-by-one in buffer alignment when cache hit path uses quantization assembler. Patch in PR #861.

Thu 2026-03-12
- Deployed continuous-batching heuristic to staging; observed p99 improvement on mixed-short workload. Started long-run soak test.
- Performance notes: fused-softmax gives greatest benefit on seq_len 256–1024; for seq_len < 32 we should prefer cuBLAS in current autotuner. Added rule to prefer cuBLAS for seq_len<=32.
- Action item: run a fleet-wide simulation (traffic replay) to estimate memory pressure from enabling KV cache for redwood-compat-7b; Samir and Lina to coordinate.

Known blockers
- Fast-attn fallback path regresses small-batch perf. Blocker for enabling fused attention on some model shapes. Owner: Benji.
- Quantized path RNG mismatch when KV cache is hot — low-severity correctness issue but must be fixed before we flip cache on for production quantized families. Owner: Maya.
- Memory guardrails for multi-tenant KV cache not finalized (size accounting + auto-eviction policies for Dedicated pools). Owner: Samir + infra.

Decisions made
- Canary rollout thresholds for new kernels (see above) established in sync.
- Autotuner will persist per-device best tile sizes under /var/lib/redwood/autotuner (short-term). Long-term plan: move to centralized store (optimize team backlog).
- Enable prefix-KV cache for gpt-medium-v2 and redwood-compat-7b in staging only until memory simulation completes.

Action items (owner — due)
- Benji — finish fast-attn fallback perf fixes and add unit/regressions (due 2026-03-19).
- Maya — merge PR #861 to fix quantization RNG mismatch and run full sampling QA (due 2026-03-16).
- Samir + Lina — run fleet replay to model memory pressure for KV cache enablement (start 2026-03-13, report 2026-03-18).
- Priya — extend kernel autotuner to include a weighted cost metric (latency + memory) and add CI microbench validation (due 2026-03-23).
- Ops — add k8s resource quota alert for KV cache memory usage > 80% (PM: Samir, due 2026-03-17).

Metrics and quick numbers (staging/replay)
- fused-softmax median token latency: down 7% (seq_len 512, batch-size 4)
- p95 token latency: down 3%
- KV cache hit-rate: 18% -> 37% for chat replay dataset (prefix heavy)
- Memory overhead: ~1.8GB per 16GB KV partition (measured)
- Mixed-short workload p99: reduced by ~14% after batching heuristic change

Notes to self / loose ideas
- Consider an indexable prefix tree for microcache to reduce avg_kv_age — might reduce eviction churn for long sessions.
- Explore probabilistic LFU variant for high-traffic tenants (avoid cold-start thrash).
- Longer term: centralize autotuner results and annotate model families so inference runtime can pick model-specific kernel profiles at request time.

Risks
- Enabling KV cache widely without robust guardrails could cause OOMs on dense Dedicated pools. Need careful simulation and OTA limits.
- Autotuner rule complexity increases code surface area — more tests and CI microbenching required.

Next week plan (Mar 13–19)
- Primary: finish fast-attn fallback regression fixes and merge quant RNG patch.
- Secondary: complete fleet memory simulation and draft rollout policy for KV cache in Dedicated.
- Tertiary: wire up CI microbench step that runs kernel-hotpath perf comparison on change to fused-softmax or autotuner.

Appendix: quick links and refs
- PRs: #842 (merged), #855 (fast-attn WIP), #861 (quant RNG fix WIP)
- JIRA: RT-341 (autotuner), RT-356 (fused-softmax variance on A100)
- Slack threads: #eng-runtime (perf), #prod-rollouts (canary alerts)

-- end of notes --
